reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows Y–Hf co-doping improves hot corrosion resistance in a high-entropy alloy coating via Al2O3 formation, but it does not address boride substrates, molten aluminum environments, or the proposed catalytic nucleation/adhesion mechanism on borides. The key premise that this mechanism transfers to boride–molten aluminum systems is unsupported.
premises: Y–Hf additions promote Al2O3 nucleation and adhesion in high-temperature corrosive environments
Y–Hf additions improve corrosion resistance by forming a protective Al2O3 scale
The mechanism observed in Y–Hf co-doped high-entropy alloy coatings applies to boride surfaces in molten aluminum
